newsitem.title: FRANCE: SGB SELLING ACCOR STAKE - FUND MANAGERS.
newsitem.headline: SGB SELLING ACCOR STAKE - FUND MANAGERS.

text.p: Societe Generale de Belgique, a subsidiary of Compagnie de Suez , is selling its eight percent stake in French hotel group Accor at 756 francs per share, fund managers said on Wednesday.
A spokeswoman for Accor confirmed the transaction, led by brokerage SBC Warburg.
"It's a good thing for us," the spokeswoman told Reuters. "It's one less sword of Damocles (hanging over us). We knew SGB might sell its shares but we didn't know when."

She said the group had been concerned about the impact of a flood of shares hitting the market. But "the sale was carried out through dispersed placements to Anglo-Saxon (British and American) investors, with each holding less than one percent," she said.
Fund managers said earlier this month they were being sounded out on their interest in Accor shares.
SGB's stake in Accor was nine percent at the end of last June.
Suez and SGB both declined to comment.
